title: Upgrade Fee Basis by Point in the Membership Year — Northgate Memberships
content:
For a mid-year upgrade of a membership of Northgate Memberships to its Plus tier, the upgrade fee is worked from the upgrade fee basis, and that basis depends on where in the membership year the upgrade falls and on whether the upgrade is a first upgrade.

## Definitions

- **Current membership year:** the membership year on the membership on the upgrade date, from its first day to its expiry date.
- **Days after the first day:** calendar days from the first day of the current membership year to the upgrade date; an upgrade on the first day is 0 days after it.
- **Whole months remaining:** whole calendar months from the upgrade date to the expiry date; a month counts only when the expiry date's day of the month has reached the upgrade date's day of the month.
- **First upgrade:** an upgrade made on a membership whose ledger carries no upgrade difference fee from any earlier upgrade.
- **Base fee paid for the current membership year:** the sum of the new membership and renewal fee charges recorded for the membership year that is current on the upgrade date, less any refunds of those charges.
- **Plus annual fee:** 130.00 dollars.
- **Difference:** the Plus annual fee less the annual fee of the tier held.

## Decision table

| Upgrade date | First upgrade | Upgrade fee basis |
|---|---|---|
| no more than 60 days after the first day of the current membership year | Yes | priced as a renewal at the Plus tier: the Plus annual fee less the base fee actually paid for the year, rounded to the cent |
| fewer than 6 whole months of the membership year remain | Yes | the difference multiplied by the whole months remaining from the upgrade date to the expiry date and divided by twelve, rounded to the cent |
| every other case | — | the difference in full |

In words: when the upgrade date is no more than 60 days after the first day of the current membership year and the upgrade is a first upgrade, the upgrade is priced as a renewal at the Plus tier, and the upgrade fee basis is the Plus annual fee less the base fee actually paid for the year, rounded to the cent. When fewer than six whole months of the membership year remain on the upgrade date and the upgrade is a first upgrade, the upgrade fee basis is the difference between the Plus annual fee and the annual fee of the tier held, multiplied by the whole months remaining and divided by twelve, rounded to the cent. In every other case the upgrade fee basis is that difference in full.

## Worked cases (hypothetical memberships; year 1 January to 31 December 2027)

| Tier held | Ledger | Upgrade date | Reading | Upgrade fee basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Club | renewal charged 58.20 for the year, no earlier upgrade | 2 March 2027 (60 days after) | first row | 130.00 less 58.20, that is 71.80 |
| Club | renewal charged 65.00, of which 6.50 refunded; no earlier upgrade | 1 February 2027 (31 days after) | first row | 130.00 less 58.50, that is 71.50 |
| Club | renewal 65.00, no earlier upgrade | 3 March 2027 (61 days after); 9 whole months remain | third row | 65.00 |
| Club | renewal 65.00, no earlier upgrade | 10 August 2027; 4 whole months remain | second row | 65.00 multiplied by 4 and divided by twelve, 21.666…, that is 21.67 |
| Heroes Club | renewal 45.50, no earlier upgrade | 1 July 2027; 5 whole months remain | second row | 84.50 multiplied by 5 and divided by twelve, 35.208…, that is 35.21 |
| Club | ledger shows an upgrade difference fee from an earlier upgrade | 20 January 2027 | third row | 65.00 |

Boundary checks: 60 days after the first day is inside the first row and 61 days is outside it; 6 whole months remaining is outside the second row and 5 is inside it.
